details: The U.S. Federal Reserve decided to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% following its July 29 meeting, marking the fifth consecutive pause in rate hikes. However, the decision was not unanimous, with three members of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) dissenting and advocating for a 25-basis-point increase, highlighting persistent concerns about inflation. Following the announcement, the U.S. dollar experienced its steepest decline in two weeks. Historically, a weaker dollar is often seen as a positive catalyst for risk assets like Bitcoin. Despite this, the cryptocurrency market displayed a largely muted reaction, with Bitcoin trading around $64,172-$64,400. Analysts suggest this subdued response indicates that the rate hold was largely priced into the market or that a prevailing defensive sentiment among traders outweighed the traditional bullish signal of a falling dollar.
title: Fed Holds Interest Rates Steady Amidst Split Vote; Dollar Dips, Crypto Muted

details: Global equity markets, particularly the technology sector, have recently experienced a significant sell-off, impacting major stocks like Nvidia and leading to a sharp drop in Nasdaq futures and South Korea's tech-heavy KOSPI index. This broad downturn in technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) linked stocks has fueled concerns about the sustainability of the recent AI investment boom and is contributing to a wider risk-off sentiment in financial markets. The pressure from falling technology stocks has made investors more cautious across the wider market, extending its influence to cryptocurrencies. The crypto market saw declines in major digital assets, with Bitcoin falling around 2.7% and Ethereum dropping more than 3.2% on July 28 amid these broader market anxieties. Some market observers suggest that capital rotating out of cooling AI and chip stocks could potentially flow into Bitcoin, provided there's sustained demand for spot BTC funds.
title: Global Tech and AI Sector Sell-off Spreads to Crypto Markets
